recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-19359 unless FHIR-I later reopens the broader modifier-extension policy; FHIR-37903 was only background for this seed and should remain separate.
issue_request: FHIR-19359 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core FHIR-I change request raised from STU3 and applied for R5. It asked to revise the extensibility page's Notes bullet about unsafe-to-ignore extensions after a clinical-safety Zulip discussion showed the text could be read too broadly. The accepted resolution was to define 'Not safe' as causing information in other elements to be interpreted inconsistently with their base definitions and to point to examples below.
initial_application: Git commit 67ee800fd2ddfec4ee1fbcc42d293789a7429077 explicitly applied FHIR-19359 by adding the requested sentence to source/extensibility.html. Later editorial changes corrected the original typo and link syntax while preserving the seed clarification.
additional_context: The #implementers Zulip thread 'Max dose per course' clarifies the rationale: modifier extensions are about changing the meaning of other elements, not generic clinical-safety importance. FHIR-I minutes deferred the tracker to R5 in October 2018 and accepted it on 2019-04-22 with a 7-0-0 motion. Later modifier-extension work such as FHIR-37903 added nearby guidance but did not supersede this clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini actively includes the extensibility page, and source/extensibility.html:71 already says that 'Not safe' means the extension causes information in other elements within the resource to be interpreted in a way that is not consistent with their base definition, with a link to the modifier-extension examples.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive modifier-extension clarification touched the same extensibility area and preserved, rather than superseded, the FHIR-19359 distinction.
